In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis and performance evaluation of multiuser systems with memoryless non-linearities at the transmitter.

developing new techniques for interference suppression in multiuser systems that are based on a generalization of the notion of interference suppression for linear systems to include the possibility for nonlinearity.

the development of a generalized concept of interference annulment and the corresponding multiuser detectors for nonlinear multiuser systems that can achieve higher performance gains over existing multiuser detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed detectors are capable of achieving a performance gain of up to 1.5 dB in the presence of nonlinearity over conventional detectors.

the proposed multiuser detectors based upon the concept of interference suppression outperform conventional multi user detectors based upon the conventional concept of multiuser interference cancellation, and the performance gain is more prominent for nonlinear multiuser systems.
the successive interference annulments (SIA) detectors proposed here are optimal for nonlinear systems and hence, are the most effective detectors for nonlinear multiuser systems in general.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed detectors are optimal or near-optimal in terms of the conditional error exponent and hence, the effective energy.

, for the first time, we have proposed and analyzed a family of multiuser detectors for nonlinear multiuser systems, which are based on the concept of successive interference suppression, which can be applied to a broad class of multiuser communication systems.

the proposed multiuser detection schemes based on successive interference suppression are optimal in the sense of maximizing the asymptotic error exponents and are also optimal in a more generalized sense of maximizing the conditional error exponent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed detectors are capable of achieving a performance gain in terms of the conditional error exponent that is not possible using the conventional detectors.
the proposed detectors are based on a general concept of interference suppression and are not restricted to any specific nonlinearity.
the asymptotic multi-user error exponent is a useful metric for comparing multiuser detectors in nonlinear systems, which is not possible using the conventional multiuser error probability.
